[[File:מיכל ציון.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Michal Zion]]
'''Michal Zion''' ({{Langx|he|מיכל ציון}}) is a professor and the head of the Biology Education Center at the Faculty of Education, [[Bar-Ilan University]]. Her scholarly work examines open [[Inquiry-based learning]] in the context of Biology education, as well as [[Environmental Literacy Plan]].

==Biography==
Michal Zion was born and raised in [[Tel Aviv]]. During her military service, she taught soldiers at [[Har Gilo]] [[Field School (Israel)|Field School]], the [[Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel]].
<ref name=" Anat Georgy ">Anat Georgy (January 23, 2023). [https://www.themarker.com/allnews/2023-01-23/ty-article-magazine/.premium/00000185-da54-d04b-abef-dbff95e10000 "Clean-up campaigns are worthless": The professor who discovered the secret to removing trash from natural sites]. ''[[TheMarker]]''.</ref> She earned her B.Sc. in biology from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. She obtained her doctorate in the School of Medicine at the Hebrew University under the supervision of Prof. Yinon Ben-Neriah.<ref>
[[:he:ינון בן נריה|Yinon Ben-Neriah]]. ''[[Hebrew Wikipedia]]''.</ref> The dissertation titled “The regulation of human [[ABL (gene)|abl gene]] expression in [[Philadelphia chromosome|Philadelphia]] positive [[Leukemia|leukemic]] cells in comparison to normal cells.”<ref name=" Michal Zion CV">
[https://www.michal-zion.com/_files/ugd/5b7641_b86882543c5e4b31936187463e9d686b.pdf Michal Zion CV].</ref> The research provides insights into the [[epigenetics]] mechanisms involved in [[Carcinogenesis|tumorigenesis]], specifically how progressive [[methylation]] [[Chronic myelogenous leukemia]], and was published in the [[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]].<ref>Michal Zion et al. (1994). [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ:u5HHmVD_uO8C Progressive de novo DNA methylation at the bcr-abl locus in the course of chronic myelogenous leukemia]. ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]''. Vol. 91. Is. 22.</ref> During her PhD studies, she received a biology teaching diploma and taught at [[Ironi He High School]], her [[Alma mater]]. 
The center for development and support for high school biology labs. Bar-Ilan University.<ref name=" Anat Georgy "/>

In 2000, Zion became a lecturer at the School of Education at Bar-Ilan University and has been affiliated ever since. In 2008, she was appointed senior lecturer; in 2014, she was appointed associate professor and the head of the Science Education Center, the Biology Education Center.<ref>[https://www.biu-edulab.org.il/about/ The Center for Development and Support for High School Biology Labs. Bar-Ilan University].</ref> As the deputy head of the School of Education, in 2003 she was appointed full professor. 2005-2006: [[Sabbatical]] fellowship at the Science and Mathematics Education Centre (SMEC), [[Curtin University]], [[Perth]], [[Australia]]. She heads The National Center for Support and Development of Biology School Laboratories, The Faculty of Education, Bar-Ilan University<ref name=" Michal Zion CV"/> In 2017, she received the rector prize for Scientific Innovation from Bar-Ilan University.<ref>[https://cris.biu.ac.il/en/prizes/rector-prize-for-scientific-innovation Rector Prize for Scientific Innovation]. ''Bar-Ilan University''.</ref>

In 2020, she initiated the environmental project and the [[NGO]]<ref>[https://takezevel.co.il/about/ About]. ''Take the garbage with you''.</ref> “Take the Garbage with you” to keep Israel's natural sites clean.<ref>Shay Elbling (September 3, 2021). [https://modiin.mynet.co.il/local_news/article/h1ul2phbf The war against piles of trash: Dozens of municipalities joined the cleanup initiative that started in Modiin]. ''Mynet Modi'in'' ([[Yedioth Ahronoth]]).</ref> She initiated various educational and environmental projects with the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] and the [[Council for a Beautiful Israel]].<ref name=" Anat Georgy "/>

Michal Zion is married, has three children,<ref name=" Anat Georgy "/> and resides in [[Modi'in-Maccabim-Re'ut|Maccabim]].<ref>(September 4, 2020). [https://modiin.mynet.co.il/local_news/article/r1qj1WaXP Taking trash into her own hands: The project from Maccabim that will make you clean up after yourself]. ''Mynet Modi'in'' (Yedioth Ahronoth).</ref>

==Research==
Michal Zion's studies focused on [[Active learning]], especially the open-inquiry-based learning and teaching approach to [[Science Studies]]. A [[review article]] published in the Educational Research Review that analyzes the current research on the open-inquiry-based approach in science teaching and learning cites six of Zion's papers among the 24 most influential papers in the field.<ref>NM Dah et al. (May 2024). [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1747938X24000101?casa_token=feZsZZy7YyUAAAAA:4zCqYzdrr8muGwinD6Qv7Rn6BJjeLdVqK07-Wevw92VKBgA7ZN3lwTxW7mXkQS3wrcy3ziR7 The impacts of open inquiry on students’ learning in science: A systematic literature review]. ''[[Educational Research Review]]''. Vol. 43. 100601. [[Elsevier]].</ref>

She discusses the shift from structured to open inquiry in science education in an article. The study explores how inquiry-based learning can simulate scientific research processes, emphasizing the need for [[Higher-order thinking|high-order thinking]] and student ownership of investigations. The model, implemented in Israeli high school biology [[Curriculum|curricula]], promotes a [[social constructivism]] approach to science education, moving away from traditional instructional methods.<ref>
Zion, M., & Mendelovici, R. (2012). [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ:ufrVoPGSRksC Moving from structured to open inquiry: challenges and limits]. ''Science Education International'', 23(4), 383-399.</ref>  In another article, Zion compares the dynamic inquiry performances of students engaged in open versus guided inquiry learning environments. The research shows that open inquiry students, involved from the early stages of the inquiry process, outperform their guided inquiry peers in dynamic inquiry performances characterized by [[Cognitive flexibility|Intellectual flexibility]] and [[critical thinking]].
<ref>Sadeh, I., & Zion, M. (2009). [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ:d1gkVwhDpl0C The development of dynamic inquiry performances within an open inquiry setting: A comparison to guided inquiry setting], ''[[Journal of Research in Science Teaching]]'', 46(10), 1137-1160.</ref> Another study examines the preferences of Israeli high school biology students between open and guided inquiry projects. The results indicate that students favor open inquiry projects, as they feel more satisfied and perceive more significant benefits despite differences in documentation efforts.<ref>Sadeh, I., & Zion, M. (2012). [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ:Y0pCki6q_DkC Which type of inquiry project do high school biology students prefer: Open or guided?], ''Research in Science Education'', 42, 831-848.</ref> Zion explored how [[Metacognition|metacognitive]] guidance and peer collaboration enhance environmental literacy. The meta-CIC model integrates open inquiry-based learning with strategies to improve students' thinking and understanding of environmental issues. The approach emphasizes reflective learning and collaboration to foster more profound engagement and problem-solving skills for ecological challenges.<ref>Adler, I., Zion, M., & Mevarech, Z. R. (2016). [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ:u-x6o8ySG0sC The effect of explicit environmentally oriented metacognitive guidance and peer collaboration on students’ expressions of environmental literacy]. ''[[Journal of Research in Science Teaching]]'', 53(4), 620-663.</ref> Another article investigates the role of curiosity in open-inquiry learning among high school students. She identified four models for establishing logical connections between inquiry questions, contributing to the open inquiry planning process. The study shows that curious students pursue inquiries with less certainty but with a higher degree of dynamic inquiry.<ref>Zion, M., & Sadeh, I. (2007). [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ:UebtZRa9Y70C Curiosity and open inquiry learning]. ''[[Journal of Biological Education]]'', 41(4), 162-169.</ref> A [[qualitative research]] analyzes the diverse teaching practices within the Israeli high school biology curriculum, Biomind, emphasizing open inquiry. The study identifies teachers' challenges in facilitating dynamic inquiry, such as limited scientific knowledge and time constraints, and suggests professional development strategies to address these issues.<ref>Zion, M., Cohen, S., & Amir, R. (2007). [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ:qjMakFHDy7sC The spectrum of dynamic inquiry teaching practices], ''Research in Science Education'', 37, 423-447.</ref> She investigates the teacher-student dynamic in the open inquiry process within the Biomind curriculum. The study highlights how teachers facilitate self-directed student learning, fostering scientific literacy, motivation, and responsibility. The findings stress the importance of collaboration between teachers and students in dynamic inquiry settings.<ref>Zion, M., & Slezak, M. (2005). [https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=tIC3NQ0AAAAJ:2osOgNQ5qMEC It takes two to tango: In dynamic inquiry, the self-directed student acts in association with the facilitating teacher], ''Teaching and Teacher Education'', 21(7), 875-894.</ref>
